newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU not ready to raise malt refund yet - source.
newsitem.headline: EU not ready to raise malt refund yet - source.

text.p: The European Commission does not currently believe an increase in the European Union's malt export refund is justified, an EU cereals management committee source indicated on Friday.
"They did not act yesterday," the source said, adding that this was a reliable indication that the Commission believed the current level of 32.50 Ecus per tonne was adequate.
The EU's cereals management committee meets in Brussels each Thursday. The source declined to predict what would happen to malt refunds at next week's meeting.
The Commission is at loggerheads with the malt industry over the refund, which exporters want raised on the grounds that underlying barley refunds have also risen.
The dispute was one of the dominant issues at a European grain industry gathering in Antwerp on Friday, traders said.
"The maltsters are thoroughly upset," said one trader. "They are impatient because they can't get on with the business."
An official with international grain trade association GAFTA said it was calling for a clear and transparent system.
"Maltsters should be able to take out licences when they want, with refunds set in line with barley. There should be no manipulation of the refund," the official said.
Malt industry sources in Brussels also called for the malt refund to be set in line with barley.

Malt exporters, backed by Britain and Belgium, argue that malt should be set at 30 percent above the prevailing barley export refund. The latest barley refund was 30.98 Ecus, implying a malt refund of 40.27 Ecus per tonne if this were accepted.
But several management committee sources argued that malt sales were currently profitable on world markets and the current refund was enough for the industry to function smoothly.
